The invention concerns a device for stunning live poultry intended for slaughter while the birds are held in containers. Stunning is carried out using a gas mixture that includes a stunning gas. The device includes a stunning chamber with at least two stunning zones, an entry-side introduction station for one or more containers holding live poultry, and an exit-side discharge station for one or more containers holding stunned poultry. It also has at least one transport conveyor that moves the container or containers in a transport direction T through the stunning zones from the introduction station to the discharge station, together with equipment for supplying the gas mixture to the stunning zones of the stunning chamber.

The invention relates to an apparatus for stunning live poultry intended for slaughter, in particular while the animals remain inside containers used for handling and transport. The apparatus is designed to allow the poultry to be stunned in a controlled manner without first having to remove the animals from the containers.

The apparatus comprises a stunning chamber through which the containers are conveyed. The stunning chamber includes at least two stunning zones, enabling the stunning process to be carried out in stages or under different gas conditions. An introduction station is provided at an inlet side of the apparatus for feeding the containers into the stunning chamber, and a discharge station is provided at an outlet side for removing the containers after the stunning process has been completed. A transport conveyor moves the containers from the introduction station, through the stunning chamber and its stunning zones, and onward to the discharge station.

During transport through the stunning chamber, a gas mixture containing a stunning gas is supplied to the stunning zones. The gas mixture is used to stun the poultry while the animals remain in their respective containers. The composition, concentration, and distribution of the gas mixture may be controlled so that the poultry are exposed to the desired stunning atmosphere for a suitable period of time as the containers pass through the different stunning zones.

The gas delivery system comprises at least one movable injection pipe. This injection pipe is configured so that it can be detachably connected to a container and subsequently detached from that container after gas has been supplied. When connected, the injection pipe delivers the gas mixture directly into the container, allowing the container itself to be filled with the gas mixture. In this way, the poultry inside the container are exposed efficiently and reliably to the stunning gas during their movement through the apparatus.

Because the injection pipe is movable and detachably connectable, it can cooperate with containers as they are transported through the stunning chamber. The connection may be made temporarily for the duration required to fill or partially fill the container with the gas mixture, after which the pipe can be disengaged and made available for connection to another container. This arrangement allows stunning gas to be introduced directly into the containers rather than relying solely on the general atmosphere within the chamber.

The invention therefore provides not only an apparatus for stunning poultry in containers, but also a corresponding arrangement and method. In the related method, containers holding live poultry are introduced into the stunning chamber, transported through at least two stunning zones, detachably connected to at least one movable injection pipe, filled with a gas mixture containing a stunning gas, and then conveyed to a discharge station after the poultry have been stunned.
outputs.L4:
The apparatus, arrangement, and method relate to the stunning of live poultry before slaughter, particularly poultry that is transported and presented for processing while still held in containers, crates, drawers, or similar receiving units. Instead of removing the birds from the containers before stunning, the system is designed to treat the poultry while they remain inside the containers, thereby reducing handling, stress, injury, and labor requirements before the slaughtering operation.

The stunning process is carried out using a controlled gas mixture, such as a gas containing carbon dioxide, inert gas, reduced oxygen, or another suitable stunning atmosphere. The containers holding the live poultry are conveyed through a stunning installation that is divided into a plurality of stunning zones. Each zone may be operated with a selected gas composition, gas concentration, exposure time, flow rate, or pressure, allowing the birds to be exposed gradually or in stages to the stunning atmosphere. This staged treatment can improve animal welfare by avoiding abrupt exposure to high concentrations of stunning gas and by ensuring that the poultry reach the required stunned or unconscious condition before further processing.

A key feature of the system is a movable injection pipe arranged to supply stunning gas directly into an individual container. The injection pipe is movable relative to the containers and is configured to be brought into engagement with a selected container when that container reaches a gas-supply position. The pipe can be detachably connected to the container, for example through an opening, coupling, inlet, valve, or sealing interface provided on the container. Once connected, the injection pipe introduces the stunning gas directly into the interior of the container, so that the birds inside that specific container are exposed to a controlled amount of gas.

After the desired filling or exposure step has been completed, the injection pipe can be disconnected from the container and moved to another container. This detachable and movable connection allows each container to be treated individually, rather than relying solely on flooding an entire chamber or tunnel with gas. As a result, gas delivery can be more accurately controlled according to the size, loading condition, position, or processing requirements of each container. The system can also reduce gas consumption and improve the uniformity of stunning, because the gas is introduced directly where the poultry are located.

In one arrangement, a conveyor transports a sequence of poultry-filled containers through the stunning zones. At one or more locations along the conveyor path, the movable injection pipe is positioned so that it can align with and connect to each container in turn. Sensors, actuators, seals, valves, and control equipment may be used to coordinate the movement of the pipe, verify the connection, regulate the gas flow, and monitor the gas concentration inside the container or zone. The pipe may be raised, lowered, pivoted, extended, retracted, or otherwise displaced to establish and release the connection automatically.

The method includes providing live poultry in containers, moving the containers into or through the stunning apparatus, connecting the movable injection pipe to a container, supplying a stunning gas mixture through the pipe into the container, maintaining the gas supply for a predetermined time or until a desired gas condition is reached, disconnecting the pipe, and then moving the container onward through subsequent stunning zones or toward slaughter. The procedure may be repeated for each container, allowing continuous or semi-continuous processing of poultry in an industrial slaughter line.

By using a movable injection pipe that detachably connects to each container, the apparatus enables direct, container-specific filling with stunning gas. This provides improved control over the stunning atmosphere, supports staged exposure through multiple stunning zones, and helps ensure that poultry are effectively and humanely stunned before slaughter while remaining in their transport or holding containers.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the most common words in the English language, yet it carries an important function. It is called the definite article, and it helps point to a specific person, place, thing, or idea. For example, when we say “the book,” we are not talking about any book, but a particular book that the speaker and listener understand.

Although “the” is a small word, it gives clarity and meaning to sentences. It helps organize communication by showing that something is already known, unique, or clearly identified. We use it in phrases such as “the sun,” “the world,” and “the best choice” to refer to something specific.

In writing and speech, “the” may seem simple, but it plays a powerful role. Without it, many sentences would sound incomplete or confusing. This tiny word proves that even the smallest parts of language can be essential.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft an invention summary in European patent style for a poultry slaughter stunning chamber with multiple zones, inlet and outlet stations, conveyors, and gas delivery means connected directly to containers.
counterfactuals.output:
### Summary of the Invention

The invention relates to a stunning chamber for poultry slaughter installations, in particular for the controlled gas stunning of poultry prior to slaughter. The stunning chamber comprises a housing defining an interior treatment space through which poultry is conveyed from an inlet station to an outlet station. Within the housing, the interior treatment space is divided into a plurality of treatment zones arranged successively in a conveying direction, each treatment zone being configured to contain a predetermined gaseous atmosphere for progressively stunning the poultry.

The stunning chamber further comprises conveyor means for transporting poultry through the treatment zones. The conveyor means may include one or more conveyors configured to support containers, crates, modules or other poultry carriers in which live poultry is received. The conveyors are arranged to move the containers from the inlet station, through the respective treatment zones, and towards the outlet station, preferably in a substantially continuous or stepwise manner.

Gas delivery means are provided for supplying stunning gas directly to the containers carried by the conveyor means. The gas delivery means may comprise gas supply lines, nozzles, manifolds, ducts or distributors positioned adjacent to, above, below or within the path of travel of the containers. The gas delivery means are arranged such that gas is introduced directly into or immediately adjacent to the containers, thereby enabling an accurately controlled gas atmosphere to be established around the poultry contained therein.

In a preferred embodiment, each of the plurality of treatment zones is provided with respective gas delivery means and/or gas control means, enabling the gas concentration in each zone to be controlled independently. The gas concentration may be varied progressively along the conveying direction, for example such that poultry first enters a zone having a relatively low concentration of stunning gas and is subsequently conveyed through one or more zones having higher concentrations. This allows gradual induction of unconsciousness and reduces stress, wing flapping and injury.

The gas used in the stunning chamber may comprise carbon dioxide, an inert gas, nitrogen, argon, a mixture of such gases, or another gas suitable for stunning poultry. Sensors may be provided in one or more zones for measuring gas concentration, temperature, humidity and/or pressure. A control unit may be connected to the sensors, the conveyor means and the gas delivery means, and may be configured to regulate the supply of gas to the respective zones in dependence on measured values and/or operating parameters of the slaughter line.

The inlet station may comprise sealing means, doors, curtains, air locks or gas barriers to reduce escape of gas from the chamber when containers enter the chamber. Similarly, the outlet station may comprise sealing means or gas recovery means to limit gas loss when containers leave the chamber. Gas extraction, recirculation or exhaust means may also be provided to maintain the desired atmospheres within the zones and to prevent uncontrolled release of stunning gas into the surrounding working environment.

By supplying stunning gas directly to the containers, the invention enables efficient use of gas and improved control of the gas atmosphere experienced by the poultry. The provision of multiple treatment zones allows a staged stunning process, which can be adapted to different poultry types, container sizes, line speeds and regulatory requirements. The arrangement further provides a compact and hygienic construction suitable for integration into existing poultry slaughter lines, while reducing gas consumption and improving animal welfare during stunning.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention relating to gas stunning of poultry in containers, where the gas mixture is introduced via at least one injection pipe movable relative to each container and detachable from it.
counterfactuals.output:
An invention in this field may be described as an apparatus and method for stunning poultry, such as chickens or turkeys, while the birds remain in transport or holding containers.

The system includes a stunning chamber or treatment zone through which one or more poultry containers are conveyed. Each container holds live birds and is adapted to receive a stunning gas mixture, for example a mixture containing carbon dioxide, inert gas, oxygen-depleted gas, or another controlled-atmosphere stunning composition.

A key feature is that the gas mixture is supplied to each container through at least one injection pipe. The injection pipe is arranged so that it can move relative to the container. For example, the pipe may be lowered, raised, advanced, retracted, pivoted, or otherwise positioned so that it enters or aligns with an opening in the container during the stunning operation. Once positioned, the injection pipe introduces the gas mixture directly into the interior of the container, improving distribution of the stunning atmosphere around the poultry.

The injection pipe is also detachable from the container. After the required amount of gas has been delivered, or after the container has passed through the stunning zone, the pipe can be withdrawn or disconnected from the container without requiring permanent attachment. This allows containers to be moved continuously or intermittently through the system and permits the same injection equipment to be used successively for multiple containers.

In one embodiment, the apparatus includes a conveyor for moving the containers, a gas supply system, valves for controlling gas flow, and actuators for moving the injection pipes into and out of engagement with the containers. The injection pipes may be configured to seal temporarily against or within gas inlet openings of the containers to reduce gas leakage. Sensors or control equipment may coordinate the movement of the pipes with the position of each container.

The invention provides a controlled way of stunning poultry directly in their containers, reducing bird handling and associated stress. The movable and detachable injection pipe arrangement allows effective gas delivery while maintaining compatibility with transport containers and automated processing lines.

## Title  
**Apparatus for Transporting Containers of Live Poultry Through a Multi-Zone Stunning Chamber and Supplying Stunning Gas to the Containers**

## Abstract  
An apparatus is provided for stunning live poultry contained in transport containers. The apparatus includes a stunning chamber having a plurality of treatment zones and a conveyor system configured to move the containers sequentially through the zones. A gas supply system delivers stunning gas to the containers by way of a detachable movable pipe. The pipe is configured to engage a container during at least part of its travel through the chamber and to direct stunning gas into the interior of the container. The pipe may be selectively detached, repositioned, or disengaged to accommodate container movement, maintenance, cleaning, or different container configurations.

---

## Detailed Description  

An apparatus for handling live poultry comprises a stunning chamber configured to receive a plurality of containers, each container holding live poultry. The stunning chamber is divided into a plurality of zones, which may include, for example, an entry zone, one or more gas introduction zones, one or more dwell or exposure zones, and an exit zone. The zones may be arranged sequentially along a path of travel of the containers.

A transport system is provided for advancing the containers through the stunning chamber. The transport system may include a conveyor, pusher, rail-guided carriage, chain drive, roller bed, belt conveyor, or other suitable mechanism arranged to move the containers along the path of travel through the respective zones. The transport system may move the containers continuously or intermittently.

A gas supply system is arranged to supply a stunning gas to the containers while the containers are located in or moving through the stunning chamber. The stunning gas may comprise carbon dioxide, nitrogen, argon, another inert or anaesthetic gas, or a mixture of gases suitable for stunning poultry.

The gas supply system includes at least one movable pipe configured to deliver stunning gas into a container. The movable pipe is detachably connectable to a gas source or manifold and is movable relative to the stunning chamber and/or relative to the path of travel of the containers. In use, the movable pipe is positioned so that an outlet end of the pipe communicates with an interior region of a container, whereby stunning gas is introduced directly into the container holding the poultry.

The detachable movable pipe may be mounted on an actuator, linkage, guide, carriage, pivot arm, telescopic support, flexible conduit, or other movement mechanism. The pipe may be configured to move between a connected or operative position, in which gas is delivered into a container, and a disengaged or retracted position, in which the pipe is spaced from the container. The detachable connection permits removal of the pipe for cleaning, replacement, maintenance, or adaptation to different container sizes or gas-delivery arrangements.

In certain embodiments, the movable pipe travels with a container for at least a portion of the container’s movement through a zone of the stunning chamber. In other embodiments, the movable pipe is inserted into or placed adjacent to a container when the container is temporarily stopped within a treatment zone. The pipe may include one or more gas outlets, nozzles, apertures, diffusers, or distribution openings positioned to distribute the stunning gas within the container.

Each zone of the chamber may be supplied with a different gas concentration, flow rate, exposure time, or gas composition. The gas supply system may include valves, sensors, flow meters, controllers, pressure regulators, gas analyzers, and control logic configured to regulate delivery of stunning gas to each container or to each zone. The apparatus may thereby provide a controlled stunning sequence as the containers move through the chamber.

---

## Example Independent Apparatus Claim  

1. **An apparatus for stunning live poultry contained in containers, the apparatus comprising:**  
   
   a stunning chamber defining a path of travel and comprising a plurality of zones arranged along the path of travel;  
   
   a transport system configured to move a container holding live poultry through the plurality of zones of the stunning chamber; and  
   
   a gas supply system configured to supply stunning gas to the container while the container is in the stunning chamber,  
   
   wherein the gas supply system comprises a detachable movable pipe having an outlet arranged to deliver the stunning gas into an interior of the container, the detachable movable pipe being movable between an operative position in which the outlet is in fluid communication with the interior of the container and a disengaged position in which the detachable movable pipe is separated from the container.

---

## Dependent Claims  

2. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the plurality of zones comprises at least two zones having different stunning gas concentrations.

3. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the plurality of zones comprises an entry zone, a gas introduction zone, an exposure zone, and an exit zone.

4. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the transport system comprises a conveyor configured to advance the container through the stunning chamber.

5. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the transport system is configured to move the container intermittently and to stop the container in at least one of the plurality of zones while the stunning gas is supplied through the detachable movable pipe.

6. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the detachable movable pipe is configured to move with the container along at least a portion of the path of travel while delivering stunning gas into the container.

7. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the detachable movable pipe is mounted to a movable support selected from the group consisting of a pivot arm, a sliding carriage, a telescopic arm, a guided rail assembly, and an articulated linkage.

8. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the detachable movable pipe comprises a quick-release coupling configured to permit removal of the pipe from the gas supply system.

9. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the detachable movable pipe comprises a flexible hose portion and a rigid outlet portion.

10. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the outlet comprises a plurality of apertures configured to distribute the stunning gas within the container.

11. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the outlet comprises a diffuser.

12. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the detachable movable pipe is configured to extend through an opening in the container.

13. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the detachable movable pipe is configured to engage a gas inlet port of the container.

14. The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a sealing member arranged around the outlet to reduce escape of stunning gas from the container during delivery of the stunning gas.

15. The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a controller configured to control a flow rate of the stunning gas through the detachable movable pipe.

27. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the transport system is configured to transport a stack of containers through the stunning chamber.

---

## Example Method Claim  

31. **A method of stunning live poultry contained in containers, the method comprising:**  
   
   moving a container holding live poultry along a path of travel through a stunning chamber comprising a plurality of zones;  
   
   positioning a detachable movable pipe relative to the container;  
   
   placing an outlet of the detachable movable pipe in fluid communication with an interior of the container;  
   
   supplying stunning gas through the detachable movable pipe and into the container while the container is within the stunning chamber; and  
   
   disengaging the detachable movable pipe from the container after supplying the stunning gas.

35. The method of claim 31, further comprising controlling a flow rate of the stunning gas through the detachable movable pipe based on a position of the container within the stunning chamber.

36. The method of claim 31, further comprising detaching the movable pipe from a gas supply manifold for cleaning or replacement.

37. The method of claim 31, wherein supplying the stunning gas comprises introducing the stunning gas through a plurality of apertures or a diffuser at an outlet end of the detachable movable pipe.

38. The method of claim 31, wherein the stunning gas comprises carbon dioxide, nitrogen, argon, or a mixture thereof.

---

## Alternative Broad Claim Language  

1. **A poultry stunning system comprising:**

   a source of stunning gas; and  
   
   a gas delivery assembly connected to the source of stunning gas, the gas delivery assembly including a movable delivery pipe detachably coupled to the gas delivery assembly and configured to be selectively positioned in gas-delivery relation with a poultry container conveyed by the container transport mechanism,  
   
   wherein the movable delivery pipe is arranged to introduce stunning gas directly into the poultry container while the poultry container is located in the chamber.
